sections.title: Why FANUC Co-Training Exists
learningObjectives: Understand DiFacto's position as an integrator of both MoRo and FANUC systems
Recognize why this makes a dual-system Master Instructor more valuable
sections.content: Many DiFacto deployments involve MoRo working alongside FANUC robotic systems. The I/O handshake integration introduced in the Programmer track (L3B-M4) reflects this reality. A Master Instructor who can train on both MoRo and the FANUC integration points it connects to is a significantly more valuable training resource than one who only knows MoRo in isolation - since real deployments rarely involve MoRo alone.

keyTerms.note: An industrial robotics manufacturer whose controllers MoRo commonly integrates with via I/O handshake.
An exchange of request, ready, and complete signals between MoRo and another machine, so each acts only when the other is ready.

sections.title: What This Module Covers
learningObjectives: Understand the general scope of FANUC-side knowledge relevant to MoRo instructors
Recognize this is integration-focused training, not full FANUC certification
sections.content: This module isn't a substitute for standalone FANUC certification. It will cover the FANUC-side knowledge specifically relevant to training others on MoRo-FANUC integration points: the I/O handshake sequence from the FANUC controller's perspective, common FANUC-side configuration that affects integration behavior, and how to explain the combined system to a learner who may be new to one side or the other. Detailed curriculum content is being co-developed with FANUC-side training materials.

sections.title: Teaching an Integrated System
learningObjectives: Understand the pedagogical challenge of teaching a system with two distinct origins
Recognize strategies for building a coherent mental model across both sides
sections.content: Teaching an integrated MoRo-FANUC workflow is harder than teaching either system alone. A learner needs a coherent mental model spanning both, not two separate, disconnected sets of knowledge. Effective instruction here means consistently connecting the two sides explicitly - what MoRo does, what the FANUC controller does in response, and why - rather than teaching them as parallel but unrelated topics.

keyTerms.note: A learner's internal picture of how the whole system works.

sections.title: Common Points of Learner Confusion
learningObjectives: Recognize typical areas where learners struggle with integrated systems
Know that anticipating this confusion and addressing it early helps
sections.content: Learners new to integrated systems often struggle most with handshake timing. They need to understand that MoRo and FANUC are each waiting on signals from the other, not acting independently. Anticipating this confusion and addressing it early, with the handshake concept already introduced in L3B-M4, gives Master Instructors a known point to reinforce rather than leaving it as an implicit assumption.

video.title: Handshake timing in 30 seconds
video.transcript: Teaching an integrated system. Learners often struggle most with handshake timing. MoRo and FANUC each wait for the other’s signal. They do not act independently. Address the confusion early. Build on the handshake from L3B-M4.

sections.title: Co-Delivery Considerations
learningObjectives: Understand what co-delivery with a FANUC-side trainer might involve
Recognize that co-delivery by two instructors may be more effective for advanced troubleshooting
sections.content: For more complex integration training, co-delivery alongside a FANUC-side trainer may be more effective than one instructor covering both sides alone - particularly for advanced troubleshooting scenarios. This module will cover how to plan and coordinate that kind of session. The specific protocol for co-delivery logistics is being finalized as DiFacto's instructor network develops.

keyTerms.note: Two trainers, such as a MoRo instructor and a FANUC-side trainer, delivering one session together.

sections.title: Certification Implications
learningObjectives: Know what completing this module signals about a Master Instructor
Recognize the value this adds to DiFacto's instructor network
sections.content: Completing this module as part of the broader L5 Master Instructor track signals an instructor capable of training on a common real-world deployment pattern - MoRo integrated with FANUC systems, rather than MoRo in isolation. This supports DiFacto's role as an integrator of both systems.

questions.question: Why does DiFacto want Master Instructors who can train on the FANUC integration points?
options: Many DiFacto deployments have MoRo working alongside FANUC systems
L5 certification includes FANUC's own certification
MoRo-only training is delivered by FANUC-side trainers
questions.feedback: Correct. Real deployments often combine both systems, making dual-system instructor capability valuable.

questions.question: Which of these is in the scope of this module?
options: FANUC-side knowledge relevant to MoRo-FANUC integration points
General FANUC robot programming beyond the integration points
questions.feedback: Correct. This module is integration-focused and is not a substitute for standalone FANUC certification.

questions.question: What makes teaching an integrated system pedagogically harder than teaching one system alone?
options: Integrated systems must be taught on separate days to keep the two sides from blurring
Learners need one mental model spanning both sides, not two disconnected sets
The two systems cannot be shown running together in a lab
questions.feedback: Correct. Building a coherent cross-system mental model is the core instructional challenge.

questions.question: A learner says, "MoRo finishes its part, then the FANUC robot just does its own thing." What does this show?
options: They see the two systems as acting independently, not waiting on each other's signals
They need standalone FANUC certification before continuing
They should be taught the two systems as separate topics first
questions.feedback: Correct. Handshake timing, where each system waits on signals from the other, is a frequent source of learner confusion.

questions.question: What does completing this module signal about a Master Instructor?
options: They can train on a common deployment pattern: MoRo integrated with FANUC
They no longer need to keep MoRo-specific knowledge current
They hold FANUC's own certification as well as DiFacto's
questions.feedback: Correct. It signals readiness to train on the combined system, not MoRo in isolation.
